name: Barbados
snapshot: A republic since 2021, where Mia Mottley, a leading global voice on climate finance, won a third term in February 2026 by sweeping all 30 seats.
culture: Barbados, settled by the English in 1627, was a sugar colony built on enslaved African labour, and its Bajan dialect, food and festivals reflect both legacies. Crop Over, a harvest festival revived in 1974, is a summer of calypso and soca ending in the Grand Kadooment parade. Rihanna, declared a National Hero in 2021, is the island's most famous daughter.
society: Barbados has high literacy and life expectancy for the region and relies on tourism and international business. It removed Queen Elizabeth II as head of state in 2021. Mottley's Bridgetown Initiative pushes the IMF and World Bank to change lending to climate-vulnerable nations.
baseline: Mia Mottley's Barbados Labour Party won all 30 seats in the February 2026 election, as it had in 2018 and 2022, giving her a third term. President Jeffrey Bostic took over as ceremonial head of state in 2025.
